explanation: The amounts cooks use change the boiling point and the heating time far too little to notice. The fizz when salt hits hot water comes from crystals giving bubbles places to form.

claims.text: Adding salt in the amounts used in cooking does not make water come to the boil noticeably faster.
Salt in cooking amounts changes the boiling point of water, and the time it takes to boil, by amounts too small to notice.
When salt is added to hot water, the crystals act as nucleation sites where bubbles form, causing a brief fizz.
